messages.subject: Single exon calling
parts:
Hello, thanks for your hard work on Codex, so far it seems to have very high accuracy for large CNV events. 

 You mention in the paper that calling single exon CNVs is possible with a simple thresholding algorithm. Do you have any example code for this, or guidance on where the normalized / fitted depths are found prior to segmentation? 
 
Thanks!
 Brendan

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] Single exon calling
parts:
Hi Brendan,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX. For single-exon CNV detection, you can take the log ratio of Y over lambda, where Y is the observed read depth after QC and lambda is the baseline normalized read depth under the null (i.e., in the case where there is no CNV).

z=log(Y_qc/Yhat[[optK]]) 

should give you this z-score. You need to be careful and sometimes conservative to choose optK though. See the bottom of our GitHub page for more details https://github.com/yuchaojiang/CODEX .

Yuchao
